# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 14 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 14 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_014_page_001.jpg

---

1 Think of it: a sailor about to venture through the violence of the sea calls out to a plank of wood even more fragile than the ship beneath his feet.

2 The ship itself was born from human greed — yet wisdom was the one who shaped it.

3 And it is your providence, Father, that steers it through, for you have opened a road even through the sea, a safe passage through the churning waves,

4 proving that you can rescue from any danger, so that even the inexperienced may cast off from shore.

5 You do not wish for your wisdom's works to lie idle — so people stake their very lives on the tiniest scrap of wood, and riding a simple raft through the surf, they arrive home safe.

6 So it was in the beginning too: when the arrogant giants were going down to ruin, the hope of the world found shelter on a raft, and, steered by your hand, preserved a seed of future generations for the age.

7 Blessed indeed is the wood through which righteousness is brought to pass.

8 But the idol carved by human hands is cursed — and so is the one who carved it. He is cursed because he made it; it is cursed because though it decays and crumbles, it was called a god.

9 God holds the ungodly and their ungodliness in equal contempt,

10 and both the act and its perpetrator will face the same punishment.

11 This is why even the idols of the nations will be called to account: in the very fabric of God's creation they have become a horror — a trap laid across the path of the foolish, a stumbling block for every soul that wanders.

12 Idol-making was the starting point of spiritual adultery; it was the invention that rotted life from within.

13 These things did not exist at the beginning of time, and they will not last until the end.

14 They crept into the world through the empty arrogance of human beings, and so a swift end has already been designed for them.

15 It began this way: a father, shattered by grief over a child snatched away too soon, made an image of the little one so quickly lost. What had been a dead human being he now honoured as a god, and handed down to those who came after him secret rites and solemn ceremonies.

16 As time passed, the godless custom hardened into law. By royal command, carved images became objects of worship.

17 And because people living at a distance could not honour the monarch in person, they imagined his face and fashioned a visible likeness — eager to flatter the one far away as though he were standing right there.

18 And the craftsman's ambition drove the cult still further, drawing in even those who had never known the king —

19 for the artist, wanting to win favour with whoever commissioned him, forced his skill to produce a likeness more beautiful than the original,

20 and the crowd, dazzled by the beauty of the work, came to worship the one they had so recently honoured merely as a man.

21 This became life's secret snare: people in the grip of grief, or crushed under tyranny, gave to stones and sticks the Name that belongs to no one else.

22 As though it were not enough to go astray about God — living in a great war of ignorance, they name such towering evils "peace."

23 They slay children in their rites, or celebrate hidden mysteries, or hold wild midnight revels with ceremonies strange and lawless —

24 and in all of this they have abandoned purity of life and purity of marriage. One person destroys another by treachery; one wounds another by adultery.

25 Everywhere the same chaos reigns: blood and murder, theft and fraud, corruption and betrayal, rioting and perjury,

26 the persecution of the innocent, ingratitude for kindness done, souls rotted through, the confusion of the sexes, disorder in marriage, adultery, licentiousness.

27 The worship of nameless idols is the beginning, the cause, and the final end of every evil.

28 These worshippers either work themselves into a frenzy of ecstasy, or they mouth false prophecies, or they live in wickedness, or they lie under oath without a second thought —

29 for since they trust in idols that cannot hear, they expect no consequences when they swear falsely.

30 But justice will catch up with them on both counts: they were wrong about God when they gave themselves to idols, and they were dishonest before God when they swore deceitfully, making a mockery of holiness.

31 It is not the power of the things they swear by that pursues them — it is the just punishment that always dogs the footsteps of those who do wrong.
